data.title: Boot Loop
data.description:
Users need to update iOS regularly to maintain the stable and smooth operation of the iPhone. However, sometimes a user may face some unforeseen problems. Like the boot loop in this instance, where the phone starts and shows the Apple logo. Then it goes black and again shows only the Apple logo on the screen; the phone can show nothing beyond that. This issue happens mostly when there is a failed or interrupted software update on your phone. Also, other issues may cause your phone to boot loop, such as:

  • Physical Damage (Dropping the phone from your hand, etc.)
  • The battery connector may have gotten loose or have gone bad.
  • Hardware Damage.
  • Improper or failed update that is missing necessary files to get the phone started.

If you think one of the above issues is causing the boot looping error on your phone, you may just try these fixes listed below and see if they work to resolve your issue.

  • Force Restart Your iPhone XS
  • (Press the volume up button, (+) then release the button. And then quickly press and release the volume down button (-) and then hold the power button again until your screen turns black and shows the Apple logo.
  • Check if your iPhone is fully charged or is charging properly.
  • Connect your iPhone to your computer and try restoring or updating the software through the iTunes application.

If your phone still doesn’t recover from boot looping after trying these fixes, something may have gone wrong that can only be fixed by a professional iPhone technician. data.description:
These are error codes that indicate to the service technicians that a specific part of the iPhone is malfunctioning. These codes are used by professional repair technicians of iPhones to make their jobs easy. They do not need to diagnose the entire iPhone when they see the code. Therefore, it saves both the customer’s and the tech expert’s time and other resources.

Some of the common error codes seen in the iPhones are as follows: ERROR(9): This code shows when you are trying to upgrade your iOS through PC on iTunes, but the iTunes app shows an error code 9. It is a relatable problem with iTunes error codes—4013, 4014, and 4005.

Apple recommends:

  • To check if your iPhone is updated
  • To check if the lightning cable works. (Error codes 4013, 4014, and 4015 usually indicate this issue.)
  • If the update still fails, try updating from another PC.
  • Error 1015: This is an issue if you have a jailbroken device (iOS) and Apple detects it.
  • Error 69: This is a common issue found in iPhone X and later devices. This issue suggests that there might be some sort of hardware error on your phone, which is repairable, to say the least.

Aside from these errors, there are a lot of errors that can occur on your iPhone. These are all listed on Apple’s error solution info pages with possible DIY (do it yourself) solutions.

data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone XS offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter how hard they try, there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones, and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

This stuck-on-Apple-logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be

  • The iPhone has taken on some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)
  • The update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss.
  • A third-party app may have access to vital permissions, which can disrupt iPhones' productivity.
  • It is rare; however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up.

These issues, however, can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if they work for you...

Force restart your iPhone XS.

(Press volume up (+) and then quickly press the volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone XS power button as long as the Apple logo appears again.)

Update your iOS software.

(If, while in the process of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, you may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted.)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install apps only from the Apple App Store.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the SIM tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the SIM tray by putting the ejector pin into the SIM tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the SIM tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the SIM tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver, then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water. However, if your LCI turns red, you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water, here are some basic things you should do:

  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth.
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY.
  • If anything spills on your phone (like oil, etc.), just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.
  • If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your battery or charging port or give you muffled speakers.

data.description:
Now you can repair your faulty touch mechanism of the iPhone Xs without having to change the entire display! Since the launch of the new iPhone X models, Apple has introduced a technology that separates the touch mechanism and upper glasses from the entire display. Therefore, users who face problems or issues in their display panels can get it looked at separately.

The iPhone XS also has a separate touch and display panel which integrates and works as a whole unit. If your phone has a faulty, unresponsive, broken, or damaged touch, you need not replace the whole display unit. ifixit bd has a dedicated service to replace or repair your touch panel (not the entire display) in-service points located all over Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Signs that indicate a faulty touch mechanism in iPhone XS are...

  • Doesn’t work or No response / Program doesn’t open or respond after touching the icon
  • Delayed response or wrong response (Clicking on one place but the phone registers the touch elsewhere and opens an unrelated app)
  • Takes multiple touch attempts to open an app or perform an action on the phone.
  • Ghost Touch / Delayed Touch issue

If you see any of the signs on your phone you can safely assume that the touch mechanism is faulty and should be replaced. Because Apple uses Haptic touch on iPhone XS and haptic touch ensures that there’s no struggle to operate the phone by touching it.

data.title: Temperature High Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone XS comes with a generally better and more efficient processor and battery than the iPhone X series. Although the users have said that the phone tends to get hotter than the previous iPhones Apple has released,. The new iPhone XS comes with a special thermal compound in the back area of the phone, which helps to omit heat faster and more efficiently than the previous iPhones. It may make your iPhone seem a lot hotter than the previous iPhones.

However, that doesn’t make the iPhone XS so warm that the users find it difficult to hold it down with their hands. This is a clear indication of overheating in the iPhone XS. Some similar cases of overheating include.

  • The phone gets way too hot while charging and takes a long time to be fully charged.
  • The phone gets hot, and the battery drains drastically.
  • You might see a notification that will say “Temperature high.”
  • The iPhone gets warm on standby mode for no apparent reason whatsoever.

(Note: if your phone gets too hot while transferring data for the first time from a previous iPhone, chances are it’s a one-time issue and will not happen again.)

These are some of the most discussed problems in Apple’s user threads and community. However, there are some DIY (do it yourself) fixes that you may try that may help you to resolve your overheating issues.

  • Disable background app refresh.
  • Disable background app refresh from here: Settings > General > Background App Refresh
  • Turn off Bluetooth/location services to reduce processes running in the background.
  • Most of the users have reported they get heating issues in the latest iOS version. In that case,
  • Try updating your iOS to later versions to check if it works for your phone.

If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get it looked at by professional technicians who specialize in resolving iPhone XS heating issues. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving your iPhone XS issues on your phone. ifixit bd is located in four different service points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone Xs comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature...

  • Face not recognized
  • Face ID is not available at the moment
  • Move the camera a bit lower/higher
  • Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID.

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

  • Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock.

Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

  • if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.
  • Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region.
  • Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy.
  • Update your iOS to the latest version.

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompt with a passcode. The reasons may be:

  • User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone.
  • The user may have just restarted the device.
  • The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours.
  • The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days.
  • The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours.
  • The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space.
  • If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts.
  • If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all.

  • Siri doesn’t work/can’t hear me/can’t pick up commands.

  • At the bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls.

  • The one in the back of you is in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video.

  • Make sure you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes.
  • Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there.
  • Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works.
  • If the mic works in voice memo, make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone XS.
  • Go to Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone.

  • Delayed Touch issue
  • Touch doesn’t respond after dropping from hand. (Everything else seems to work fine.)

  • Make sure there’s no internal/external damage (cracking or shattering glass).
  • Disconnect your USB-lightning port to check if it works.
  • If your phone is above normal temperature, wait for it to cool down and then try again.
  • Restart your device.

  • The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked-out phone. Therefore you can not determine the problem
  • iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.

  • Limit background processes by stopping background app refresh

data.title: Audio Issue
data.description:
It has two speaker grills in the bottom part of the phone. It should be kept in mind that the left speaker grill is not a speaker, but instead it is there to catch audio inputs for your voice calls and Siri. The audio only comes out of the right speaker grill, and it is not a faulty feature. The two speakers of the iPhone XS are located on the top and the bottom of the phone. The top speaker also serves its purpose as an ear speaker when in calls.

However, some users have reported a lot of different audio issues. The most common audio issues faced by iPhone XS users are

  • No sound in audio playback
  • No sound in voice calls
  • Distorted sound/low sound on the speakers
  • Headphones not working
  • Audio not working or audio levels low after an update.
  • Phone stuck in headphone mode
  • Ringer switch not working/audio level increases or decreases automatically/physical audio level buttons not working.

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. Those are

  • Checking the ringer switch to see if it is on the sound mode
  • Restarting Your Phone
  • Disabling your Bluetooth in the iPhone XS
  • Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode.
  • Check sound notification settings and try turning noise cancellation off.
  • Try using headphones and check if the sounds come through okay in headphones.
  • Try removing any protective cases.
  • Clean the speaker grills of dirt and debris.

If none of the fixes works for your phone, you need to get it checked by professional technicians who specialize in repairing iPhones. In ifixit bd, we have experienced technicians who specialize in repairing iPhone XS. Our service points are located at locations in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
